text: In the days of David there was a famine that lasted three years, year after year, and David sought the face of the LORD. The LORD said, "It is because of Saul and his bloodstained house, because he put the Gibeonites to death."

versions.text: In the days of David there was a famine that lasted three years, year after year, and David sought the face of the LORD. The LORD said, "It is because of Saul and his house of bloodshed, because he put the Gibeonites to death."
versions.explanation: "his house of bloodshed" is a stiff calque of בֵּית הַדָּמִים and stumbles when read aloud. "his bloodstained house" carries the same sense (a household guilty of bloodshed) with a smoother rhythm.

text: So the king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites but a remnant of the Amorites, and the Israelites had sworn an oath to spare them; yet Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for Israel and Judah.
David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? How can I make atonement, so that you will bless the inheritance of the LORD?"

The Gibeonites answered him, "It is not a matter of silver or gold between us and Saul or his house, nor is it for us to put any man in Israel to death." David said, "Then what do you say I should do for you?"

versions.text: The Gibeonites answered him, "It is not a matter of silver or gold between us and Saul or his house, nor is it for us to put any man in Israel to death." David said, "Whatever you say, I will do for you."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מָה־אַתֶּם אֹמְרִים אֶעֱשֶׂה לָכֶם is most naturally an interrogative ("What are you saying I should do for you?"), which also fits the narrative flow, since the Gibeonites only state their demand afterward in vv. 5-6. Rendering it as a promise ("Whatever you say, I will do") anticipates the king's consent, which comes at the end of v. 6.

text: They said to the king, "As for the man who consumed us and plotted to destroy us, so that we would not survive anywhere in the territory of Israel—
let seven of his sons be handed over to us, and we will hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD." The king said, "I will hand them over."
But the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

So the king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul—Armoni and Mephibosheth—and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite. [^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew text reads *Michal*; since Adriel married Saul's daughter Merab (1 Samuel 18:19) and Michal had no children (2 Samuel 6:23), some ancient manuscripts and many interpreters read *Merab* here.

versions.text: So the king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul—Armoni and Mephibosheth—and the five sons of Merab daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew text reads מִיכַל (Michal). Silently substituting "Merab" changes the source text without any indication to the reader. Either follow the Hebrew with an explanatory footnote (as suggested) or, if "Merab" is retained, a footnote must state that the Hebrew reads "Michal."

text: He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged them on the hill before the LORD. All seven of them fell together; they were put to death in the first days of the harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

Then Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on the rock. From the beginning of the harvest until the rain poured down on the bodies from the heavens, she did not let the birds of the sky settle on them by day or the wild animals by night.
When David was told what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, had done,

he went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of his son Jonathan from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hung them on the day they struck Saul down at Gilboa.
He brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of his son Jonathan, and they also gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.

They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the land of Benjamin, at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father, and they did everything the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer on behalf of the land.
Once again there was war between the Philistines and Israel. David went down with his servants, and they fought the Philistines; and David grew weary.
Then Ishbi-Benob, one of the descendants of the Rapha, whose bronze spearhead weighed three hundred shekels and who was armed with a new sword, intended to kill David.

versions.text: Then Ishbi-Benob, one of the descendants of the Rapha, whose bronze spearhead weighed three hundred shekels and who was armed with a new sword, said he would kill David.
versions.explanation: וַיֹּאמֶר with an infinitive here means "determined/intended" rather than a spoken statement; "said he would kill David" reads as reported speech and weakens the sense of imminent danger that Abishai's rescue answers in v. 17.

text: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine down, and killed him. Then David's men swore to him, "Never again will you go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished."
Some time later there was another battle with the Philistines, at Gob. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, one of the descendants of the Rapha.
In yet another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
And there was another battle, at Gath, where there was a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He too was descended from the Rapha.
When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimeah, David's brother, struck him down.
These four were descendants of the Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his servants.
